title: A delivery-acceptance request that never names a skill loads project-verifier, and the answer names the missing entry point
prompt: 按工作区的 REQUIREMENTS.md 逐条验收这份交付：每条给出满足或不满足的结论和核对依据。不要修改任何文件。

fixture.notes: Three requirements, all unmet in different ways: no /health route (only /status and /version), retry attempts is 2 instead of 3, and run.sh does not exist.

graders.expects: every read_skill call used name=project-verifier; no other workflow was loaded instead
the answer names run.sh, the requirement that is unmet because the file does not exist
graders.evidence: final assistant text against the fixture tree and REQUIREMENTS.md

graders.expects: the answer names /status, so the route claim comes from app.py rather than from the requirements text
graders.evidence: final assistant text against app.py's ROUTES

cleanup: Discard the trial workspace; the fixture directory is never written to.
notes: Every requirement is unmet, so an answer that reports three passes is wrong on the fixture's own facts; the two text graders only check that the answer reached the file tree and the route table, not that its per-item reasoning is sound. The distinguishing claim remains the skill read, which nothing in the prompt names. Per-item verdict quality stays semantic and unasserted.
